saints.name: St. Brigid of Ireland
saints.title: Abbess
saints.shortBlurb: The great abbess of Kildare, honored with Patrick and Columba as a patron of Ireland, whose boundless charity to the poor filled the memory of her people…
biography: Born about 451 at Faughart near Dundalk, the daughter of the chieftain Dubhthach and Brocca, a Christian slave, Brigid gave away so much of her father's goods to the poor, once even his jewelled sword, that the King of Leinster, recognizing her holiness, bade her father set her free. She received the veil and consecrated her virginity to God.

About 480 she founded the monastery of Kildare, the 'church of the oak', a double house of women and men which she governed as abbess with Conleth as its bishop. It grew into a centre of religion and learning, with a school of art whose illuminated Book of Kildare later drew the wonder of Gerald of Wales.

Her earliest life, written by the monk Cogitosus about 650, brims with tales of charity and of butter and milk multiplied for the poor, whence she is a patron of dairymaids. She died at Kildare on 1 February about 525, and her nuns long kept a fire burning in her honour. With Patrick and Columba she is a patron of Ireland, called the Mary of the Gael.
saints.knownFor: Her monastery of Kildare and her legendary charity to the poor.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 1 February
